title: fix: keep Gateway responsive during plugin tool discovery
body:
Closes #188031

## What Problem This Solves

Opening the plugin tool catalog can freeze unrelated Gateway activity while plugin discovery performs a synchronous registration chain.

Reported and originally fixed by @ctbritt; the contributor's commits and production repair are retained.

## User Impact

Other Gateway requests can progress between plugin registrations while `tools.catalog` loads. Optional and unresolved tool rows, requested-agent workspace, metadata ownership, name conflicts and sorting remain intact. Individual synchronous plugin callbacks still block for their own duration; this is not a general latency guarantee.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog reuses its Gateway generation's already-admitted load context and metadata with the existing asynchronous inspection owner instead of repeating synchronous preparation. It retains generation authority, projects rows within inspection lifetime, awaits resource release, then checks authority before publishing success. Standalone inspection retains settled owners so failed registration cannot trigger synchronous fallback reload.

No new cache, registry manager, timeout, service, dependency, permission or persisted schema is introduced. No authentication, SDK, product configuration, prompt or update paths change.

## Evidence

[Independent built-Gateway main/candidate WebSocket comparison and regression receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188033#issuecomment-6523979099).

Independently installed and built pinned main `1891469e2bf5bf68f2de45c2683bfa59ad200448` and contributor candidate `da27dd52ad37718bad16f67aa8d6e09a7317f241` in secretless Docker with Node 24.22.1. The maintainer follow-up changes tests, documentation and isolated benchmark tooling only; production catalog/inspection bytes match the proven candidate.

A real authenticated protocol-4 WebSocket client requests `tools.catalog` from the compiled Gateway, then sends `health` after the first actual synthetic registration begins. Twelve local plugins each perform 80 ms of synchronous registration work, armed only after normal Gateway startup. Later registrations inspect a marker written only after the client receives health, so an initial yield or cleanup-only yield cannot satisfy the proof.

| Ref / independent cold run | Health received | Catalog completed | Catalog pending at health | Later registrations observe delivered health |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| main / 1 | 1015.67 ms | 1002.10 ms | no | 0 |
| main / 2 | 1071.19 ms | 1017.74 ms | no | 0 |
| candidate / 1 | 393.26 ms | 1267.47 ms | yes | 8 |
| candidate / 2 | 324.54 ms | 1154.05 ms | yes | 9 |

All runs return **12/12** optional tools. Core-only catalog + health controls succeed on both refs without invoking plugin registration. These are injected plugin workloads, not measurements of the reporter's live installation, Control UI, or a model turn. No account or paid model key was used.

The existing catalog suite now uses real loader/inspection fixtures rather than separate mocked projection and real-loader suites. It preserves responsive registration ordering, failed-registration settlement, disposal/revocation, requested workspace, metadata/conflict/sort/schema projection, no tool execution, producer/cleanup failure and core capability contracts.

- Main regression: **1 failed /5 skipped**, specifically `[false, false]` instead of `[false, true]` between registrations; wrapper 8.74 s.
- Candidate owner and consumers: **89 passed** across catalog, MCP registration and optional-plugin files; wrapper 26.96 s. Final owner rerun after style consolidation: **6/6**, wrapper 9.83 s.
- Targeted lint and formatting pass. Native mock-ledger prune shrinks 6476 → 6475; the baseline only shrinks.
- Whole-PR production **+130/-95 (net +35)**; tests **+237/-237 (net 0)**; docs **+5**. The new test file and test-lines allocation are removed; no allowance expands.
- [Benchmark consumer repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188033#issuecomment-6524227876): the existing synthetic copy-measurement tool now supplies async inspection/lifecycle fixtures and awaits warmup and measured calls. Counts (`--expect-copies 0`), timing and allocation modes each pass with one iteration; focused lint/format pass. Tooling delta **+11/-5 (net +6)**.

The contributor's earlier real built-Gateway trace independently observed health delivery during registration; the comparison above adds the pinned-main negative cases and repeated controls.

## Merge Risk

**Two-way door:** a revert restores synchronous catalog discovery; no configuration or persisted-data migration is written. Blast radius is plugin catalog inspection, including registration/factory lifetime and cleanup. Generation revocation must not publish a stale catalog, and optional declarations or metadata must not disappear; the real owner-boundary tests retain those checks. Individual plugin callback CPU work remains synchronous.
